verdict.rationale: Orb's own docs show hybrid fixed-fee-plus-usage subscriptions configurable in the web UI, with minimums and maximums, seat quantities, add-ons, prepaid credit allotments with top-ups, and credit-balance tracking. However, the specific tiered, volume, graduated and per-unit price models named in the story are never documented in the pack. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of tiered, volume, graduated and per-unit pricing models, explicit commitment/overage constructs, and independent hands-on corroboration of no-code configuration.

support.subject: As a finance lead, I can price with tiered, volume, graduated, per-unit, and hybrid subscription-plus-usage models — including credits, commitments, and overage — without custom code

citations.quote: Minimums: Ensures a minimum charge is applied. Maximums: Caps the charge at a certain amount.

Subscription Edits let you change a single subscription's pricing configuration directly from Orb's web interface or via the API - add or remove add-ons, update fixed-fee quantities (seats), apply or edit discounts, maximums, minimums, and schedule effective dates
Customers can either buy tokens on-demand, or set up an automatic top-up to buy tokens on their behalf when they're depleted.
whether you're using flat-rate subscriptions, usage-based pricing, pricing on seats, or you've implemented custom billing logic
